findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a consignment of single-used food containers in boxes stored on the floor in the hallway. Discuss with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that they will get them store properly. The consignment had just been delivered the day before and had to be temporarily stored at the observed location.  Ensure that single-used articles are stored in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash and other contaminants. Singles-used articles shall be stored at least 6” above the floor always.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: Inspector observed 3 boxes of food on the floor of the walk in cooler. Ensure that the food is stored off of the floor.

(A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Measuring spoons, cups, and other utensils are observed to be stored in a tub with soil and food crumbs in the bottom. Dump the tubs and clean on a regular basis to avoid this issue. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.comment:
The wall behind the 3 part sink is in disrepair.  Repair and seal the wall behind the 3 part sink. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

Observed multiple spray bottles of quat to not have common name labeled on the bottles. Inspector provided black marker. Bottles were labeled, “sanitizer”. Discussed having spray bottles labeled with common name with the PIC. Ensure staff is aware. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed the following non-food contact surfaces in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Large build-up of food splash, grease, etc behind the ovens and grills at the prep line. Equipment needs pulled out and floors throughly cleaned.
2. Baffles of the hood system and metal wall behind grills/ovens has layer of grease/residue build-up.
3. Wall next to oven (metal cart with spices in front of it - look left when observing prep line with grills/ovens) has food splash - clean wall.
4. Majority of metal shelving carts utilized for food prep (smaller carts) have build-up of food splash, grease, and dust - power wash carts.
5. Larger metal shelving carts holding cookware have small accumulations of dust.
6. Floor fan (for air cooling of kitchen) has accumulation of dust - blowing towards prep area.
7. Fan above reach-in freezer along prep line has significant accumulation of dust.
8. Ceiling vents have dust throughout kitchen - clean.
9. Food splash present on outside of multiple reach-in coolers/freezers.

Facility kitchen is in need of a good deep cleaning after busy summer season. Employee’s should take some time cleaning the highlighted areas and any other areas throughout kitchen in need of cleaning - wash, rinse, sanitize. Due to the significant amount of cleaning needed, a 10 day follow-up inspection is being issued versus correcting by next routine inspection. Next routine inspection would be in Spring 2023 due to eligibility to waive the 3rd inspection in 2022. Kitchen should be cleaned throughly before that time. Inspector will follow-up on 9/2/22.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handler’s licenses for multiple employees. PIC indicated employee’s had been working for over 30 days of employment. Ensure employee’s complete licensure and copies are kept at the facility. All food handler’s that are not certified food protection manager’s must complete training within 30 days of employment.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements. Provided copy of employee health reporting agreements. Provided copy of requirements for diagnosed food service employees and requirements for symptomatic employees for reporting, exclusion, and restriction. Inspector will follow-up on signed documentation on 6/2/21.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed multiple items at one of the front prep cooler to be out of temperature: diced chicken, diced ham, spring mix, cut lettuce, rice, sauces. Multiple items probed at 46-50 degrees F. Items were all voluntarily discarded during inspection. Prep cooler was turned down. Inspector will follow-up with temperature of prep cooler on 5/26/21. PIC is to maintain temperatures with probe thermometer until serviced.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

(REPEAT) Observed certified food protection manager's to not have proof of allergen training. Provided paperwork to complete certification. Ensure records are kept with licenses and available during the next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/6/20.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Toaster oven (food contact surface) is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed front toaster oven to have a large accumulation of debris. PIC stated that toaster oven is routinely cleaned 1x a week on Tuesday's, after meal prep day (Monday). Discussed possibility of 2x cleaning a week. COS.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-201.11  (P) Quat spray bottle was stored next to tortillas. Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. Employee moved materials to separated storage. Reference 7-201.11.

Observed quat spray bottle to be stored next to tortillas under the prep counter at front. PIC moved spray bottle away from food and food prep area. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

Observed lack of quat test strips during inspection. PIC had a food handler go to GFS during inspection to obtain quat test strips. Test strips were available by close of inspection. COS.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
PA 100-0367 (C) All CFPMs at a high risk facility should have completed an ANSI accredited allergen awareness program.

PIC stated CFM has taken allergen awareness training; however certificate was not readily available at time of inspection. PIC stated that certificate will be available upon next routine inspection. Allergen paperwork provided for other CFM's to complete training.
